competitive_landscape: ACTV vaporetto, Alilaguna and a large water-taxi fleet operate the city today — total demand proof. The wake-damage regulation is a differentiated environmental fit no displacement hull can match. No foiling incumbent.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire lagoon — San Marco, Murano, Burano, Torcello, Lido and the Marco Polo airport transfer — all very short hops where low wake matters most.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR is not required in the lagoon; the entire addressable network is short-haul Pioneer II.

precedents.why_it_matters: A city organised around boat transport with a clear ride-and-environmental upgrade thesis — though Venice's wake regulation makes it even stronger.

regulatory_note: Italian flag / EU; RINA certification; Comune di Venezia + ACTV control the regulated lagoon; strict moto-ondoso speed/wake limits. A wake-reducing electric foiler aligns directly with municipal protection policy — the regulatory case is a feature, not a barrier.
seasonality: Year-round (Venice is a year-round destination), with tourism peaks spring and autumn; the transport base is non-seasonal.
signature_routes: Marco Polo Airport ↔ San Marco (Pioneer II)
summary: Venice is unique: the lagoon is the entire transport network (vaporetto, water taxi, freight), and the moto ondoso (boat-wake) problem is a documented, regulated threat to the city's foundations — strict speed and wake limits apply citywide. A hydrofoil that lifts its hull clear of the water dramatically reduces wake at speed, making Navier an unusually strong regulatory-and-environmental fit on top of a massive tourism and airport-transfer market (Marco Polo airport ↔ San Marco).
tagline: The textbook hydrofoil case — a city where boats are the only transport and wake damage is a regulated emergency.
